title: Configuration and Code Divergence in Long-Lived Dev Branches
damaged_code:
```yaml
# Stored on feature/new-database-schema branch for 6 months
db_migrations_config:
  run_legacy_fallback: false # Merging this directly to trunk causes outages
```
pattern: Maintaining environment or behavior configurations across long-lived development branches separate from the master branch.
why_bad: Creates severe merge conflicts. It forces developers to resolve complex divergence under pressure, leading to untestable configuration states that crash when merged into trunk.
detection: A repository containing configuration files modified on branches that are multiple weeks behind trunk.
counterexample: Merging features continuously using Trunk-Based Development, using runtime flag-guarding in trunk rather than branches.
fix: Adopt trunk-based development; keep features hidden behind dynamic flags in the main branch, permitting continuous deployment of inactive code.
source: Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright - *Software Engineering at Google_ Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 16.
